exposure: obstetric diagnosis vs. non-obstetric diagnosis for ICU admission
outcome: timing of ICU admission (postpartum vs. antepartum)
cohort: Pregnant and postpartum women admitted to the ICU at the University Hospital Federico II of Naples between January 2008 and December 2013
finding: Patients admitted to the ICU with an obstetric diagnosis had a higher incidence of previous cesarean section, hysterectomy, hemodynamic instability, postpartum admission, higher TISS-28 scores, and greater need for endotracheal intubation compared to those admitted with non-obstetric diagnoses.
mod_finding: Patients admitted with an obstetric diagnosis had a higher incidence of at least one previous cesarean section.
